title: Clear cell carcinoma of the uterine corpus arising in long-standing adenomyosis after menopause: a case report

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Clear cell carcinoma of the uterine corpus arising in long-standing adenomyosis after menopause: a case report》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0030】Ovarian cancer, particularly endometrioid carcinoma and clear cell carcinoma (CCC), is well known to arise from ovarian endometrioma [1]. However, endometrial carcinoma arising in adenomyosis (EC-AIA) is exceedingly rare, accounting for less than 1% of all endometrial cancer cases [2], [3]. CCC reportedly comprises 6–14% of EC-AIA cases [3], [4]. As EC-AIA develops within the myometrium without involvement of the endometrium, abnormal uterine bleeding may be absent and cervical and endometrial cytology are frequently negative, rendering the preoperative diagnosis challenging [3], [4]. This report describes a rare case of CCC arising in long-standing adenomyosis diagnosed after menopause and is presented in accordance with the CARE reporting guideline.

【Case Presentation · p0035】A 60-year-old woman (gravida 1, para 0) presented for evaluation following the incidental discovery of a pelvic mass. The patient was 164 cm tall and weighed 49 kg, with a body mass index of 18 kg/m2. Medical history included hypertension and benign paroxysmal positional vertigo; she had never smoked.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Clear cell carcinoma of the uterine corpus arising in long-standing adenomyosis after menopause: a case report》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Case Presentation · p0050】Laparotomy was performed for suspected ovarian malignancy. Intraoperatively, a myoma-like mass was found in the posterior wall of the lower uterine corpus. A multilocular cystic mass was also observed in the left ovary. Dense adhesions, consistent with chronic pelvic endometriosis, were present among the posterior uterine mass, the anterior surface of the rectum, and the multilocular left ovarian mass (Fig. 2A). Gross examination of the right adnexa and left fallopian tube was unremarkable. A small amount of serosanguinous ascites was present in the pouch of Douglas. Since the mass was determined to be of uterine origin, the patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Gross examination of the resected specimen (Fig. 2B) revealed that the posterior lower uterine mass contained brown mucinous material, while the endometrium appeared unremarkable. The left ovary was multilocular and filled with clear serous fluid.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Clear cell carcinoma of the uterine corpus arising in long-standing adenomyosis after menopause: a case report》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · f0005】Fig. 1 Serial pelvic MRI findings over a 20-year interval. (A) Sagittal T2-weighted image obtained approximately 20 years before presentation, showing a cystic lesion at the same anatomical site as the current uterine lesion. (B) Sagittal T2-weighted image. (C) Axial diffusion-weighted image showing high signal intensity in the solid component of the mass. (D) ADC map demonstrating decreased ADC in the corresponding area. (E) Axial contrast-enhanced T1-weighted image showing enhancement of the solid component. Arrowheads: mass; arrows: solid component. MRI, magnetic resonance imaging; ADC, apparent diffusion coefficient.

【Fig. 2 · f0010】Fig. 2 Intraoperative and gross findings. (A) Intraoperative view showing a myoma-like mass in the posterior wall of the lower uterine corpus (arrow), a multilocular cystic mass in the left ovary (arrowhead), and the anterior surface of the rectum (asterisk). Dense adhesions are present among these structures. (B) Cut surface of the hysterectomy specimen showing tumor tissue within the mass in the posterior wall of the lower uterine corpus, while the endometrium (arrowheads) shows no apparent lesion.

【Fig. 3 · f0015】Fig. 3 Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings of clear cell carcinoma. (A) HE staining (×40) showing multiple foci of transition from benign adenomyosis to clear cell carcinoma (arrows). (B) HE staining (×100) showing a representative focus of transition from benign adenomyotic epithelium to clear cell carcinoma (arrow). (C) HE staining (×100) showing tumor cells with clear cytoplasm growing in tubulocystic and solid patterns. (D) HE staining (×200) showing hobnail cells. (E) Immunohistochemistry analysis for ER, showing positive staining in adenomyosis (arrowheads) and negative staining in clear cell carcinoma (arrows). (F) Immunohistochemistry analysis for HNF-1β, showing positive staining in clear cell carcinoma (arrows) and negative staining in adenomyosis (arrowheads). HE, hematoxylin-eosin; ER, estrogen receptor; HNF-1β, hepatocyte nuclear factor-1β.
